a.title: Kentucky Civil Liberties Union plans court action on behalf of Associated Students
a.body: The Herald reported the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union planning court action on behalf of Associated Students, under a headline that also named The Fly, a separate WKU underground newspaper active that year. The archive does not yet hold the article's text, so the underlying dispute is not yet confirmed.

b.title: Associated Students endorses the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union lawsuit
b.body: The Herald reported that Associated Students formally endorsed the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union's lawsuit, a month after the Herald first reported the union planning court action connected to the organization and The Fly.

a.title: Moore questions freshman candidates' campaign spending
a.body: President Bob Moore publicly questioned how freshman class candidates were spending their campaign money. The Herald ran an editorial the same week, 'Bob Moore's Comment Isn't Good Politics,' pushing back on his remark.

b.title: 'A$G?' - Moore questions freshman campaign spending
b.body: President Bob Moore publicly questioned spending by freshman candidates, in a story the Herald headlined 'A$G?'. The paper answered with an editorial arguing that Moore's comment was not good politics, and Moore wrote back disputing it.

a.title: ASG appoints a council to decide disputes
a.body: ASG appointed a council to decide internal disputes. The same issue reported that the regents bill, changing how the student regent was chosen, had passed the state House.

b.title: ASG sets up a council to settle its own disputes
b.body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had appointed a council to decide disputes inside the organization. The story ran two weeks after the same reporter, Kevin Francke, covered the resignation of ASG president Marcel Bush.

a.title: Student government conference set for the weekend
a.body: The Herald announced that a student government conference would run from Friday through Sunday. The notice appeared in the 26 March 1987 issue.

b.title: ASG prepares to host the second statewide student government conference
b.body: The Herald reported on 26 March 1987 that ASG would be host, from the following day through Sunday, to the second annual statewide student government conference, at the American Plaza on Scottsville Road. President Tim Todd expected about 50 student leaders, against about 65 at the first conference, which ASG had also hosted, and said hosting would cost between $400 and $500. Registration was $18 and the conference was open to all students. Saturday seminars were to cover leadership, communication and financial aid, with the Council on Higher Education flying in a financial aid consultant from Washington and sending its director, Gary S. Cox.

a.title: ASG bill funds a "President for a Day" fundraiser
a.body: The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-09-F, providing for a "President for a Day" fundraiser.

src.label: SGA Legislation, Bill #91-09-F, "President for a Day"

b.title: ASG bill funds renovation of its own chambers
b.body: The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-03-F, providing for the renovation of the ASG chambers.

a.title: A new store on campus
a.body: SGA proposed a new store on campus, reported by the Herald in early March as the organization kept generating campus improvement ideas through the spring.

b.title: A campus store proposal followed
b.body: SGA proposed a new store on campus, the Herald reported, as the association kept generating campus improvement ideas through the spring. A week earlier the paper had covered its wish to see the next university president promoted from within.

a.title: SGA lines up against plus/minus grading
a.body: SGA members voiced concern at their Tuesday meeting over a plus/minus grading system proposed in the University Senate by economics professor Brian Strow. Bradley said he planned to oppose it, reporting that the state's other student body presidents had urged him to fight it, and the Academic Affairs committee prepared a student questionnaire on the change. Chief Justice Troy Ransdell argued the system would penalize students who scored best.

b.title: SGA unanimously passes legislation against plus/minus grading
b.body: SGA unanimously passed legislation at its Tuesday meeting objecting to a proposed plus/minus grading system. Economics professor Brian Strow was to formally propose the system to the University Senate that day.

a.title: Two senators removed for absences; ten faced judicial review
a.body: Ten of SGA's 36 senators were called before the judicial board during the fall semester for excessive absences from senate and committee meetings. Two of them, Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston, were dismissed from the senate after failing to attend their judicial hearings, which the council interpreted as intent to resign. The rest received warnings, and Stephens said he would appoint replacements to the two empty seats.

b.title: Ten of 36 senators face judicial review; two dismissed for absences
b.body: Ten of SGA's 36 senators were called before the judicial board that semester for excessive absences from committee and full senate meetings. Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston were dismissed after failing to attend their judicial hearings; Justice Chris Jankowski said each had between eight and 10 absences. Chief Justice David Spalding said the council interpreted not appearing at a review as intent to resign.

a.title: Senate unanimously opposed the bi-term and per-credit-hour tuition proposal
a.body: SGA unanimously passed a resolution opposing an administration proposal to emphasize bi-term courses and shift tuition to a per-credit-hour model. Dodds argued the change would charge students more, since full-time students then paid for 12 hours but could enroll in up to 18. He called it a financial burden students should not have to bear.

b.title: SGA resolution opposes bi-term calendar and per-credit-hour tuition
b.body: The Tuesday meeting centered on a resolution opposing the administration's bi-term proposal, which would have put students in 80-minute classes on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays. President Gary Ransdell had said the change would let students take a full load plus a summer or winter course and graduate in three years. President Cory Dodds objected chiefly to the companion shift to per-credit-hour tuition, which he said would charge students more.

a.title: Senate tabled a plus-minus grading resolution
a.body: Senator Hannah Garland's resolution to adopt plus and minus grades for high and low letter grades was tabled after public relations chair Mac Mullins argued for a more formal proposal and more student input first; a similar plan had drawn SGA resistance when the provost proposed it in 2007.

b.title: Plus-minus grading resolution tabled with a student ballot floated
b.body: SGA tabled a resolution for a plus-minus grading system that would add plus and minus grades to As, Bs, Cs and Ds. Author Hannah Garland, chair of the Academic Affairs committee, said the system would make GPAs more exact and might make WKU more competitive. President Cory Dodds said the executive board had discussed putting the question directly to students on the spring ballot.

a.title: Executive Council nullified judicial appointment amendment
a.body: An amendment stripping the SGA president's sole power to appoint judicial council justices and raising the number of justices to seven passed at the Tuesday meeting, over Boka's objection that it bypassed presidential appointment and the senate. After the meeting the Executive Council reviewed the constitution and determined too few senators had attended for the vote to count, sending the amendment back to first read. The SGA office also temporarily moved to Garrett after flooding in Cravens.

b.title: Executive council voids an amendment stripping the president's judicial appointments
b.body: After review, SGA declared unconstitutional an amendment that had passed at its Tuesday meeting removing the president's sole power to appoint judicial council justices and expanding the council to seven justices. President Keyana Boka said the president is elected by the student body to make appointments in all three branches and said she was wary of the direction. Chief Justice Seth Church argued that vesting appointments in the executive branch as a whole created a fairer system.

a.title: Fall election drew 742 voters and seated 17 senators
a.body: SGA announced its fall election results around 12:20 a.m. in the Senate Chamber of Downing Student Union. There were 742 voters and 17 senators were elected, including three freshman senators led by Emily Pride with 281 votes. President Nicki Seay called the election very competitive, noting not everyone who ran won a seat.

b.title: 742 vote in fall election as 17 senators are elected
b.body: SGA announced fall election results around 12:20 a.m. before a crowd of about 15 people in the DSU Senate Chamber, with 742 voters and 17 senators elected. President Nicki Seay said the election was competitive and not everyone who ran won a seat. Emily Pride led the freshman senators with 281 votes, and the senators-elect were sworn in at the Sept. 30 meeting.

a.title: Veto override failed; alcohol policy resolution passed
a.body: At the final meeting of the fall semester, the senate failed to overturn the Executive Cabinet's veto of the smoke-free resolution, and President Nicki Taylor read the cabinet's official veto statement citing enforcement, housing requirements and practicality. The senate then passed Resolution 13-14-F, supporting amendments to WKU's alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct to let students 21 and older purchase and possess alcohol on campus. Co-author Jody Dahmer called the existing policy ineffective and hard to enforce fairly.

b.title: Senate fails to override the smoking veto and passes an alcohol resolution
b.body: A motion to overturn the Executive Cabinet's veto of the smoke-free resolution failed at the final meeting of the semester, which ran two and a half hours. President Nicki Taylor read the cabinet's official statement, which cited enforcement, housing requirements and practicality as the reasons for the veto. The senate passed a resolution supporting changes to WKU's alcohol policy the same night.

a.title: SGA budget fell by $19,500
a.body: SGA's budget dropped $19,500 from the previous year, largely because a $15,000 private donation was not repeated and the university cut another $4,500 in reallocations. Organizational funding took the hardest hit, losing $9,000, and scholarship pools for Academic Affairs and Student Affairs each fell by more than $5,000. Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reallocated $4,000 from organizational aid back into scholarships to soften the loss.

b.title: SGA budget falls by $19,500
b.body: SGA's budget dropped $19,500 from the prior year after a $15,000 private donation was not repeated and the university cut a further $4,500. Organizational funding took the largest hit, losing $9,000, and Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler moved $4,000 from organizational aid back into scholarships. The Herald noted WKU's SGA budget stood at $138,500 against the University of Louisville's $1.2 million.

a.title: Senate voted to disapprove Confucius Institute approval process
a.body: The Student Senate voted overwhelmingly to pass a resolution disapproving of how the Confucius Institute building project was approved, after President Gary Ransdell signed the contract in China in December 2014 and the Board of Regents, including the Student Regent, voted on it more than a month later without full details disclosed. Richey said the vote was not meant to set a precedent beyond ensuring the Board had full information before acting.

b.title: Senate votes 21-4 to disapprove Confucius Institute building process
b.body: The senate passed Resolution 2-15-F disapproving of what it called the nontransparent procedure by which the Model Confucius Institute building was authorized. Several senators argued the institute was an asset to WKU and Bowling Green, while Campus Improvement Chairman Zachary Jones backed the resolution as an expression of student opinion. Richey wrote separately that some senators had warned the vote would make "powerful enemies" for SGA.

a.title: Senate asked WKU to cancel classes on Election Day
a.body: SGA unanimously passed Resolution 5-18-F asking the university to cancel classes on Nov. 6, 2018, so students could get to the polls, after a presentation by Francis Wilson of the get-out-the-vote campaign Reg 2 Vote, and approved $300 in support through Bill 7-18-F. The senate also passed Resolutions 1-18-F and 2-18-F, which asked WKU to strike code-of-conduct language barring students from refusing a direction from a university official and from audio recording student-faculty meetings. Mayer's nominee Alex Rivera was confirmed as associate justice of the Judicial Council 12-3 after an earlier nomination had failed.

b.title: Senate asks WKU to cancel classes on Election Day and to let students record meetings
b.body: Resolution 5-18-F, urging cancellation of classes for the Nov. 6 midterms, passed 15-0 alongside Bill 7-18-F giving $300 to the Reg 2 Vote campaign. Student Francis Wilson told senators that of 290,000 Kentucky students registered in 2016, only about 13 percent voted. Resolutions 1-18-F and 2-18-F, seeking removal of Student Code of Conduct clauses requiring compliance with university officials and banning audio recording of student-faculty meetings, both passed 14-0.

a.title: Senate passes Resolution 4-19-F against Alpha Xi Delta
a.body: The senate voted 24-7 to pass Resolution 4-19-F, authored by senators Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance, supporting disciplinary action up to suspension from Greek affairs against the Epsilon Kappa chapter of Alpha Xi Delta. The resolution followed an August Twitter video showing AXiD members singing a racial slur in a rap song, and the authors said administrative silence signaled the university did not care about minority students. Before passage the senate amended the title to drop a call for outright removal from campus.

b.title: Senate passes Resolution 4-19-F seeking discipline against Alpha Xi Delta, 24-7
b.body: After a motion stripped "Removal from Campus" from the title and a friendly amendment substituted "Suspension from Greek Affairs," the senate passed the resolution 24-7. Authors Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance said they wanted more than "an article from the Herald or an email from Bob Skipper." Senator Mary Mayo said it was not SGA's job to act as a disciplinary committee; the resolution was to be submitted to the Faculty Senate.

a.title: SGA backed renaming buildings tied to racism and funded a community garden
a.body: The senate passed legislation by Brenna Matthews and Tess Welch offering SGA's support to the Naming and Symbols Task Force in changing the names of WKU buildings with ties to racism or injustice. Matthews said ties to slave owning and the Confederate army did not belong on a campus committed to diversity. Senators also unanimously funded a community garden outside the Office of Sustainability and allocated $3,500 to four student organizations.

b.title: Senate endorses renaming buildings with ties to racism and funds a community garden
b.body: A bill by Brenna Matthews and Tess Welch offering SGA support to WKU's Naming and Symbols Task Force in renaming buildings tied to racism or injustice passed after debate. Matthews said ties to slave-owning and the Confederate army were not something a public university dedicated to diversity would want on campus. Title IX coordinator Deborah Wilkins opened the meeting by reviewing previous SGA legislation that potentially violated Title IX.

a.title: Resolution condemning critical race theory bans passed 16-15
a.body: After weeks of debate, the senate passed Resolution 7.21f, which condemned the banning of critical race theory teachings in postsecondary education ahead of an anticipated bill in the Kentucky legislature. The vote was 16 in favor, 15 against, with two abstentions. Sponsor Olivia Blackmon said the measure was meant to ensure intellectual freedom in the curriculum.

b.title: Critical race theory resolution passes by one vote
b.body: Resolution 7.21f, condemning the banning of critical race theory teaching in postsecondary education, passed 16-15 with two abstentions. Sponsors cited an upcoming bill request in the Kentucky General Assembly; sponsor Olivia Blackmon said the purpose was to ensure intellectual freedom in the curriculum rather than politicize classrooms. The vote followed several speeches of affirmation and negation.

a.title: Fall election turnout doubled; Reed appointed to state council
a.body: Fall 2022 election results announced at midnight seated Rush Robinson, Callison Padgett and Rhett Helland as freshman senators, plus Neel Patel for Gatton Academy, Shy'Ante Williams as graduate senator and Salvador Leon Golib as international student senator. President Bornefeld said the vote total rose from 398 the previous fall to 805. SGA also announced that Vice President Garrison Reed had been appointed student representative on Kentucky's Council on Postsecondary Education, with a term running through June 30, 2023.

b.title: Fall election turnout doubles; vice president appointed to state postsecondary council
b.body: President Cole Bornefeld reported the fall election drew 805 votes against 398 the previous fall. Rush Robinson, Callison Padgett and Rhett Helland were elected freshman senators, with Neel Patel for the Gatton Academy, Shy'Ante Williams for graduate students and Salvador León Golib for international students. SGA also announced Executive Vice President Garrison Reed had been appointed student representative to Kentucky's Council on Postsecondary Education, with a term ending June 30, 2023.

a.title: First bill of the year funds the Pink Walk
a.body: The 23rd Senate passed its first piece of legislation, Bill 1-23-F, at its fifth meeting. The bill allocated $500 from SGA's scholarship budget for the SGA Pink Walk, an October breast cancer awareness event for students and the Bowling Green community. It passed unanimously with 28 votes.

b.title: First bill of the 23rd Senate funds the Pink Walk
b.body: The Senate passed Bill 1-23-F, allocating $500 from the SGA scholarship budget to the October Pink Walk for breast cancer awareness. The money covered bracelets, ribbons, water and raffle prizes. The bill was written by Donte Reed, Rush Robinson and Anne-Marie Wright and passed 28-0.

a.title: Senate backs Myanmar flag, funds organizational aid and calculators
a.body: The Senate unanimously passed Resolution 5-24-F backing a Myanmar flag on the empty pole outside the Mahurin Honors College, sought by senators after students said Burmese and Chin students had no flag representing them; Bill 9-24-F distributed $10,000 in fall Organizational Aid funding across 58 graded applications; and Bill 10-24-F added $540 to buy five more calculators for the Borrow-a-Calculator program, which had lent 28 calculators that semester. Kurtz appointed freshman Emaun Riley as ISEC senator and Mahurin Honors College senator Caden Lucas as the Senate's parliamentarian.

b.title: Senate backs Myanmar flag at Honors College, distributes $10,000 in aid
b.body: Resolution 5-24-F, authored by Senator Van Zing, supported flying the flag of Myanmar on the empty flagpole outside the Mahurin Honors College after Burmese and Chin students said they had no representation there. Bill 9-24-F distributed the fall organizational aid budget of $10,000 among registered student organizations graded from 58 applications, with a $500 annual cap per group. Bill 10-24-F added $540 for five more calculators after 28 had been borrowed that semester.
